title: Agent Invocation Failed Event
description: An agent invocation terminated with a non-recoverable error. See bloodbank/docs/event-naming.md.

error_code.description: Machine reason. The Hermes gateway uses processing_failed, processing_cancelled, route_policy_invalid_before_dispatch, turn_timeout (the lane's per-turn wall clock expired and the gateway stopped the turn, or a turn that detached at that clock was still running at the lane's detached ceiling; see elapsed_seconds, timeout_seconds, timeout_source, turn_stopped and detached), hermes_refused (Hermes did not run the turn: it refused it with a notice a retry cannot fix, or kept refusing it until the command had no deliveries left; see refusal), hermes_turn_error (a turn ran and Hermes ended it with an error notice such as a provider rate limit instead of an answer; see refusal) and interrupted_by_shutdown (the turn was still running when Hermes' stop drain ran out and Hermes cut it off or cancelled it at adapter teardown: it did not finish and partial work may have run; see interrupted_by and elapsed_seconds).

context.description: Echo of the originating bloodbank.agent.invocation.start or .invoke command's data.context, verbatim. Ticket turns carry reason (ticket-grooming|ticket-delegation), repo, ticket_key, ticket_id, board_id, workspace, title and phase so consumers can act statelessly. Omitted when the command carried no context.

lane.description: Delivery lane of the originating command: batch (bloodbank.agent.invocation.start) or interactive (bloodbank.agent.invocation.invoke). Stamped by the Hermes gateway on every lifecycle fact; absent on facts written before the interactive lane existed.

elapsed_seconds.description: turn_timeout and interrupted_by_shutdown: seconds between dispatching the turn to Hermes and stopping it (turn_timeout) or Hermes cutting it off (interrupted_by_shutdown). Also set on any failure of a turn that detached (seconds from dispatch to its close).

timeout_seconds.description: turn_timeout only: the wall-clock budget that expired (the lane limit, a shorter data.deadline_seconds from the command, or the lane's detached ceiling).

timeout_source.description: turn_timeout only: where the expired budget came from: the lane's turn_timeout_seconds, the command's data.deadline_seconds, or detached_ceiling (the turn detached at the lane limit and was still running at extra.interactive.detached_ceiling_seconds after dispatch; it already ran that long, so a consumer should not re-run the prompt).

turn_stopped.description: turn_timeout only: true when Hermes confirmed the turn is no longer running (session idle) after the gateway's stop; false when the stop could not be confirmed and the turn may still be unwinding.

refusal.description: hermes_refused and hermes_turn_error only: what Hermes answered instead of running the turn. A Hermes i18n notice key (gateway.busy.another_turn_running, gateway.busy.drain_queued, gateway.unknown_command, gateway.busy.drain_rejected_new_work, any gateway.errors.* key such as gateway.errors.generic_failed_with_hint or gateway.errors.context_overflow, ...), agent.operation_interrupted (the agent loop's own 'Operation interrupted ...' line was the whole reply), or the gateway's own reason: gateway_restarting / gateway_shutting_down / gateway_external_drain (Hermes was draining when the command came up for dispatch), not_accepted (Hermes' ingress dropped the event without admitting it) and not_accepted_slash_command (the prompt began with / and Hermes ran it inline as a slash command instead of an agent turn).

interrupted_by.description: interrupted_by_shutdown only: gateway_restart when Hermes was restarting (reload or restart request), gateway_shutdown when it was stopping.

detached.description: true when the turn outlived its lane's wall clock and ran on detached (it published bloodbank.agent.invocation.detached; for a voice memo this is a late reply). Absent on a turn that never detached.

detached_after_seconds.description: Detached turns only: seconds between dispatch and detaching (the lane limit).

model_override.description: Only when the command carried data.model: what became of it. requested = the route asked for; applied = Hermes switched this turn to it (/model <route> --once); reason when not applied: disabled (allow_model_override false), session_busy, switch_timeout, switch_failed:<error>, rejected (Hermes refused the route; detail quotes its reply).
